paragraphs.text: When Saul’s sin was now grown ripe and ready for the sickle, and David as a weaned child was now fitted for the kingdom.
paragraphs.anchor: And it came to pass in those days.

paragraphs.text: This struck cold to David’s good heart, who now began to repent him, doubtless, of gadding about Gath; but all too late.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt go out with me to battle.

paragraphs.text: But whether for Achish or against him, he saith not. Indeed, he could do neither with any honesty, and therefore he maketh a double answer; equivocating, as he had done before. {1Sa 27:9} Josephus is out when he saith that David did readily promise Achish his help; for what show soever he made, he meant nothing less, but prayed and hoped that God would extricate him out of this labyrinth, as also he did, {1Sa 29:3-7} so that he neither fought against Israel, nor was false to Achish.
paragraphs.anchor: Surely thou shalt know what thy servant can do.

paragraphs.text: Captain of my bodyguard. Wicked men will sooner trust the saints, than those that are graceless. Natural conscience cannot but stoop to the image of God stamped upon the hearts and lives of the religious.
paragraphs.anchor: Thee keeper of mine head.

paragraphs.text: See 1Sa 25:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Now Samuel was dead.

paragraphs.text: This is one of the dues of the dead - viz., to be sowed in the earth, and watered with tears. Mors mea ne careat lachrymis.
paragraphs.anchor: And all Israel had lamented him.

paragraphs.text: The bodies of the saints, being the temples of the Holy Ghost, should with reverence be commended and committed unto Christian sepulture, in hope of the resurrection.
paragraphs.anchor: And buried him in Ramah.

paragraphs.text: This he had done, according to Lev 19:31 Lev 20:6; Lev 20:27, at the beginning of his reign, say some, or else when for a show of his great zeal he slew the Gibeonites, {2Sa 21:1} as others hold. His seeking to these kind of creatures again therefore in his extremity, was a sin against conscience; it was point blank against verity, equity, and piety, as Junius observeth.
paragraphs.anchor: And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits.

paragraphs.text: A city in the tribe of Issachar, ennobled afterwards by the good Shunamite with whom Elisha hosted. {2Ki 4:8}
paragraphs.anchor: And pitched in Shunem.

paragraphs.text: Baleful and baneful to Saul and his sons: and therefore cursed by David. {2Sa 1:21}
paragraphs.anchor: Pitched in Gilboa.

paragraphs.text: "The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness surpriseth the hypocrites": and they run away, if they could tell whither, with these words in their mouths, "Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? Who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?" {Isa 33:14} God himself answereth in the next word. {Isa 33:15} "He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly," &c. But Saul was none such; and therefore in his extreme fear he runneth from God to the witch, and from the witch to the sword’s point.
paragraphs.anchor: He was afraid.

paragraphs.text: Those that cannot fear for love, shall once tremble for fear: and God shall laugh when such a one’s fears cometh. {Pro 1:26}
paragraphs.anchor: And his heart greatly trembled.

paragraphs.text: Which he did not with a true heart, {Heb 10:23} and Ficta pro factis non habentur, saith the Civilian: Nec videtur fieri quod non legitime fit: hence {1Ch 10:13-14} it is said that Saul inquired not of the Lord. He did, and he did not, because not uprightly nor constantly: and Nihil dicitur factum quamdiu aliquid superest faciendum. He should have persisted in seeking God, and not have run to light a candle at the devil, as they say: a sin, whereof his own hands wrought the revenge.
paragraphs.anchor: And when Saul inquired of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: And no wonder: since it was only extremity of distress that sent Saul to seek God; like as the drowning man catcheth at that bow which he contemned standing safe on the bank.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord answered him not.

paragraphs.text: For Saul had slain those that wore the ephod: and Abiathar who had it was fled to David. {1Sa 23:6} That Saul now sent to Abiathar, is a conceit of the Rabbins.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor by Urim.

paragraphs.text: He cared not for them in his prosperity, and now can have no comfort from them in the day of his distress. Let such look to it as slight God’s faithful ministers.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor by prophets.

paragraphs.text: One Rufus I read of, who painted upon his shield, God on the one side, and the devil on the other, with this inscription, Si tu me nolis, iste rogitat, If thou refuse me, here is another that will be glad of me. {a} Saul seemeth to be like-minded.
paragraphs.anchor: Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit.

paragraphs.text: “ Flectere cure nequeat superos, Acheronta movebit. ” - Virg.

So Oedipus in Seneca, when he could not get an answer at the oracles, made use of necromancy. This great sin Saul added to all his former, and so became miserable by his own election. {Jon 2:8} The like is recorded of Julian the apostate.

Heb., The dame of a familiar, such as could raise up the dead as they imagined. So Lucan {b} saith that a woman of Thessally raised up a soldier lately dead, who declared unto Pompey the evil success of the Pharsalian battle. That the woman here mentioned was Abner’s mother, may pass for a Jewish fable. Josephus saith she was vilis operaria, a poor painstaker.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit.

paragraphs.text: {a} Animi impii vox. - Piscat.
{b} Lib. 6.
As well he might with shame enough, thus to return to his vomit, and make use of those whom he had formerly suppressed. A hypocrite will at length be detected, that he may be detested.
paragraphs.anchor: And Saul disguised himself.

paragraphs.text: This speech could not choose but beat hard upon Saul’s evil conscience, making it sound heavily, as a Shaulm, but to little purpose.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done.

paragraphs.text: The Hebrews say he cut them off because they also foretold the ruin of his family, and the succession of David in the kingdom. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: How he hath cut off those, &c.

paragraphs.text: A good and seasonable answer to Satan, soliciting us to evil. We should cut him up short in such a case, as Christ doth the Pharisees, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites? and as Solomon did his mother interceding for Adoniah, Ask for him the kingdom also.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life?

paragraphs.text: {a} Lyra.
A most wicked abuse of God’s holy name: but this was ordinary with Saul, whom we have before noted for a great swearer and forswearer.
paragraphs.anchor: And Saul sware to her by the Lord.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Spectrum Samuelis, an apparition of Saumel. Saul neglected to hearken to Samuel while he was alive, and now would fain advise with him after his death. Haec est fortuna eorum qui salutaria monita spernunt. Let such look to it as despise wholesome counsel, while they may have it. "The days will come when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it." {Luk 7:22} Wherefore bestir you as good husbands.
paragraphs.anchor: Bring me up Samuel

paragraphs.text: That is, The devil in Samuel’s mantle. Who also told her that it was Saul, whence her outcry.
paragraphs.anchor: And when the woman saw Samuel.

paragraphs.text: He then was not an eye-witness at first, the witch being in secretario, saith the Gloss, in a secret place by herself, working her feats.
paragraphs.anchor: For what sawest thou?

paragraphs.text: i.e., Some goodly apparitions sent by Satan, as his apparitors and forerunners. Or, I saw a judge, or an excellent person, ascending, &c. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: saw gods ascending out of the earth

paragraphs.text: {a} Jun.
Heb., What is his form? for as yet Saul saw him not; though soon after he both saw him, and heard him preaching his funeral sermon.
paragraphs.anchor: What form is he of?

paragraphs.text: The clothes of a prophet, wherein also Samuel was buried, saith Lyra: but that is doubtful. Many great Papists hold it a gay business to be buried in a Franciscan or Dominican habit: and some at point of death have given great sums for licence to be buried in a cardinal’s purple robe.
paragraphs.anchor: And he is covered with a mantle.

paragraphs.text: This was what the devil chiefly aimed at: and it is well observed that everyone that consulteth with Satan worshippeth him, though he bow not. Neither doth that evil spirit desire any other reverence than to be sought unto.
paragraphs.anchor: And he stooped with his face to the ground.

paragraphs.text: This the true Samuel would never have said; sed ut specie Samuelem ita verbis mentiebatur diabolus, but as the devil had personated Samuel in his form, so now he doth in his words.
paragraphs.anchor: Why hast thou disguieted me?

paragraphs.text: Whereupon all mischiefs came rushing in upon him, as by a sluice. See Hos 9:12. {See Trapp on "Hos 9:12"}
paragraphs.anchor: And God is departed from me.

paragraphs.text: Samuel himself could not have spoken more gravely, severely, divinely, than this fiend doth. {a} Well may lewd men be good preachers; well may hypocrites make a great flaunt; well, it may be, that in charms and spells there is nothing to be found but good words and good prayers; of which, nevertheless, one well saith, Si Magicae, Deus non vult tales: si piae, non per tales.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore then dost thou ask of me?

paragraphs.text: {a} Dr Hall.
i.e., To him you knew of, to David his darling. Or, The Lord hath done for himself, that is, for the accomplishment of his own counsels.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord hath done to him

paragraphs.text: This disobedience the devil had once tempted him unto, and now he layeth it in his dish to drive him to despair. This is yet his method to this day: be not ignorant of his wiles.
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: See how Satan layeth load enough upon this already despairing wretch, that he may hurry him to hell: as afterwards he did the Gergesenes’ swine into the sea headlong. Till men have sinned, Satan is a parasite; when they have sinned, he is a tyrant. What careth he to flatter any more, when he hath what he would!
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the Lord will also.

paragraphs.text: That is, Shortly hence, as Exo 13:14 Mat 6:24.
paragraphs.anchor: And tomorrow.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In the state of the dead. Hereby also this old deceiver would persuade Saul that the souls of all men, as well good as bad, go to the same place: seeking thereby to blot out of him all knowledge and apprehension of eternal life.
paragraphs.anchor: Shalt thou and thy sons be with me

paragraphs.text: This the devil could not certainly foretell, though he might gather much, and give a shrewd guess, unless he had it by revelation from God, as 1Ki 22:21-22.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord also shall deliver.

paragraphs.text: Like an ox, totus totus, quantus quantus; Heb., In the fulness of his stature: and this he made haste to do. {a} Let such as run to witches look for no more comfort in distress: or else to any other like sinister practice. Clement V, Pope, sent to a wizard to know how it fared with a nephew of his, who had been his catamite, now that he was dead. The wizard assured the messenger that he had seen him in hell torments. The Pope was so troubled and terrified hereat, that he never looked up again, but died soon after. {b} Cicero {c} made lamentable moan in his misery, crying out, O me nunquam sapientem! &c. O meam cadamitosam et praecipitem senectutem! O turpem exacta dementique aetate canitiem!
paragraphs.anchor: Then Saul fell straightway all along.

paragraphs.text: Haply, saith Martyr, because such as came to inquire of witches were to come fasting; as God will be sought to by fasting and prayer.
paragraphs.anchor: For he had eaten no bread.

paragraphs.text: {a} Corruit ut erat erectus et stabat. - Vat.
{b} Jacob. Rev., in Vit. Pontif.
{c} Epist. ad Octav.
Though she were a wicked woman, yet she was not without pity and humanity, as some savages are.
paragraphs.anchor: And the woman came unto Saul.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Some such poor fare as I have at hand.
paragraphs.anchor: Let me set a morsel of bread before thee

paragraphs.text: If the message of death made Hezekiah weep, {Isa 38:3} and the approach of it was mar mar, bitter bitterness, {Isa 38:17} what wonder if Saul were so dismayed that he had no mind to his meat?
paragraphs.anchor: I will not eat.

paragraphs.text: That he might go safe out of her house, and she not be questioned for his death, as she might have been if he had there swooned quite away. Josephus highly commendeth her for this her courtesy to Saul: as also he doth him for his valour in dying in defence of his country. But so did the Decii, Curtii, and other Romans of old: and so do those Turkish desperadoes the Spahyes at this day.
paragraphs.anchor: And she hasted, and killed it.
